details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tekton Pipelines. A tenant with permissions to create TaskRun or PipelineRun resources can exploit this vulnerability. By omitting the Git API token parameter and pointing the serverURL to an attacker-controlled endpoint, the system-configured Git API token (such as a GitHub Personal Access Token or GitLab token) can be sent to the attacker. This information disclosure allows for the exfiltration of sensitive API tokens.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/tektoncd/pipeline: Tekton Pipelines: Information disclosure of Git API token via user-controlled serverURL
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate impact information disclosure flaw affects Tekton Pipelines. A user with permissions to create TaskRun or PipelineRun resources could exfiltrate the system-configured Git API token by directing the serverURL to an attacker-controlled endpoint and omitting the token parameter. This vulnerability doesn't affect a couple of Red Hat supported products as it's using a Pipelines version previously from 1.0.0, where the affected code is not present.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: It is recommended that existing users of Red Hat OpenShift Builds 1.9.z upgrade to 1.9.2

To mitigate this issue, ensure that the Git API token parameter is always explicitly provided when configuring Tekton Pipelines. Additionally, restrict permissions for creating TaskRun or PipelineRun resources to only trusted users to limit the attack surface. Review and enforce policies that prevent the use of user-controlled serverURLs without proper token authentication. Configuration changes may require a restart or reload of affected services to take effect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tekton Pipelines, a system for declaring continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines. An authenticated user, able to submit `ResolutionRequest` objects, can exploit a vulnerability by injecting malicious commands into the git resolver's revision parameter. This allows for the execution of unauthorized programs on the resolver pod. Successful exploitation can lead to the exfiltration of all cluster-wide secrets, resulting in significant information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/tektoncd/pipeline: Tekton Pipelines: Arbitrary code execution and secret exfiltration via malicious git commands
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This Important flaw in Tekton Pipelines allows an authenticated user to achieve arbitrary code execution on the resolver pod by injecting malicious commands into the git resolver's revision parameter. This vulnerability happens because the `revision` parameter is passed as a positional argument to the `git fetch` command without any previous validation whether the parameter's value doesn't start with `-` character. Combining this lack of validation with the fact the function which validates the repository URL explicitly allows a repository URL to being with `/`, translating to a local filesystem. An attacker with enough privileges to perform an operation which trigger resolvers to use the `ResolutionRequest` function can 
chain both behaviors to trick Tekton Pipelines to load and execute an arbitrary binary on the resolver pod.

Exploring this vulnerability may be considered of a high complexity as an attacker needs to either know an existing valid git repository located at a predicable path already in the resolver pod or a default URL configuration pointing to a local filesystem's path.
 
A successful exploitation of the flaw can lead to the exfiltration of all cluster-wide secrets, posing a significant risk to the integrity and confidentiality of the OpenShift environment. Additionally, depending on the data included in the `kubeconfig` files, an attacker may achieve privilege escalation or perform lateral movements within the targeted cluster.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending an HTTP request containing a Range header with a large number of small byte ranges. When the server processes these ranges while serving content, it consumes an excessive amount of CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive to legitimate users.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated with an Important severity for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server compute resources over the network, leading to a complete service outage. However, exploitation is restricted to applications that actively listen on the network and serve content using standard library HTTP handlers that process multi-range requests. CLI utilities and server components that do not handle byte-range requests from untrusted clients remain unaffected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tekton Pipelines. A tenant with permissions to create TaskRun or PipelineRun resources can exploit this vulnerability. By omitting the Git API token parameter and pointing the serverURL to an attacker-controlled endpoint, the system-configured Git API token (such as a GitHub Personal Access Token or GitLab token) can be sent to the attacker. This information disclosure allows for the exfiltration of sensitive API tokens.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/tektoncd/pipeline: Tekton Pipelines: Information disclosure of Git API token via user-controlled serverURL
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate impact information disclosure flaw affects Tekton Pipelines. A user with permissions to create TaskRun or PipelineRun resources could exfiltrate the system-configured Git API token by directing the serverURL to an attacker-controlled endpoint and omitting the token parameter. This vulnerability doesn't affect a couple of Red Hat supported products as it's using a Pipelines version previously from 1.0.0, where the affected code is not present.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details: It is recommended that existing users of Red Hat OpenShift Builds 1.9.z upgrade to 1.9.2

To mitigate this issue, ensure that the Git API token parameter is always explicitly provided when configuring Tekton Pipelines. Additionally, restrict permissions for creating TaskRun or PipelineRun resources to only trusted users to limit the attack surface. Review and enforce policies that prevent the use of user-controlled serverURLs without proper token authentication. Configuration changes may require a restart or reload of affected services to take effect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tekton Pipelines, a system for declaring continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines. An authenticated user, able to submit `ResolutionRequest` objects, can exploit a vulnerability by injecting malicious commands into the git resolver's revision parameter. This allows for the execution of unauthorized programs on the resolver pod. Successful exploitation can lead to the exfiltration of all cluster-wide secrets, resulting in significant information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/tektoncd/pipeline: Tekton Pipelines: Arbitrary code execution and secret exfiltration via malicious git commands
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This Important flaw in Tekton Pipelines allows an authenticated user to achieve arbitrary code execution on the resolver pod by injecting malicious commands into the git resolver's revision parameter. This vulnerability happens because the `revision` parameter is passed as a positional argument to the `git fetch` command without any previous validation whether the parameter's value doesn't start with `-` character. Combining this lack of validation with the fact the function which validates the repository URL explicitly allows a repository URL to being with `/`, translating to a local filesystem. An attacker with enough privileges to perform an operation which trigger resolvers to use the `ResolutionRequest` function can 
chain both behaviors to trick Tekton Pipelines to load and execute an arbitrary binary on the resolver pod.

Exploring this vulnerability may be considered of a high complexity as an attacker needs to either know an existing valid git repository located at a predicable path already in the resolver pod or a default URL configuration pointing to a local filesystem's path.
 
A successful exploitation of the flaw can lead to the exfiltration of all cluster-wide secrets, posing a significant risk to the integrity and confidentiality of the OpenShift environment. Additionally, depending on the data included in the `kubeconfig` files, an attacker may achieve privilege escalation or perform lateral movements within the targeted cluster.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go standard library packages `crypto/x509` and `crypto/tls`. During the process of building a certificate chain, an attacker can provide a large number of intermediate certificates. This excessive input is not properly limited, leading to an uncontrolled amount of work being performed. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) condition, making the affected system or application unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the Go standard library's certificate chain building process. Systems utilizing Go applications that process untrusted TLS certificates or X.509 certificate chains are susceptible to resource exhaustion when presented with an excessive number of intermediate certificates, potentially leading to service unavailability. This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

cwe.name: Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).

This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package within Go (golang). When verifying a certificate chain, excluded DNS (Domain Name System) constraints are not correctly applied to wildcard DNS Subject Alternative Names (SANs) if the case of the SAN differs from the constraint. This oversight could allow an attacker to bypass certificate validation, potentially leading to the acceptance of a malicious certificate that should have been rejected. This issue specifically impacts the validation of trusted certificate chains.

The vulnerability arises from an incorrect application of excluded DNS constraints to wildcard DNS Subject Alternative Names (SANs) when their case differs from the constraint. This could lead to Red Hat products accepting malicious certificates from otherwise trusted chains, compromising the trust model.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

This flaw impacts applications directly using `crypto/x509` or `crypto/tls`.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the internal/syscall/unix package in the Go standard library. If the target of the `Root.Chmod` function is replaced with a symbolic link during execution, specifically after `Root.Chmod` checks the target but before acting, the `chmod` operation will be performed on the file the symbolic link points to. This issue can bypass directory restrictions and lead to unauthorized permission changes on the filesystem.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: internal/syscall/unix: Root.Chmod can follow symlinks out of the root
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, an attacker needs access to the system and the required permissions to create a symbolic link. Additionally, the attacker must swap the target file with a symbolic link in the exact window after the `Root.Chmod` function checks its target but before acting. Due to these conditions, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

When verifying a certificate chain, excluded DNS (Domain Name System) constraints are not correctly applied to wildcard DNS Subject Alternative Names (SANs) if the case of the SAN differs from the constraint. This oversight could allow an attacker to bypass certificate validation, potentially leading to the acceptance of a malicious certificate that should have been rejected. This issue specifically impacts the validation of trusted certificate chains.

This could lead to Red Hat products accepting malicious certificates from otherwise trusted chains, compromising the trust model.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). Applications that validate the ASCII form then convert to Unicode may grant access to a restricted hostname the ASCII check would have rejected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http: golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect Punycode label processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. An attacker who can supply a Punycode hostname that passes an ASCII-only authorization check may have it normalized to a restricted ASCII name the application intended to block. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

Successful exploitation requires a specific set of circumstances, including the use of a proxy that relies on these headers for authentication and a user being enticed to interact with a malicious URL. The vulnerability does not allow for arbitrary code execution or a direct compromise of system integrity or availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. The compiler fails to correctly check for integer overflow or underflow in arithmetic operations involving loop induction variables. As a result, the compiler allows invalid memory indexing to occur at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: possible memory corruption after bound check elimination
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is only exploitable in applications that contain a loop structure that relies on an induction variable. An induction variable is a variable that gets modified, usually incremented or decremented, by a predictable amount on each iteration. Inside the loop, the induction variable must be directly used as the index to access or modify elements within an array or a slice. Additionally, an attacker must be able to cause an integer overflow or underflow in the induction variable to trigger this issue. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP CONNECT request with a request body is rejected by a server, the client transport can desynchronize the connection before returning it to the shared idle pool. In shared reverse proxy environments, a remote attacker can exploit this issue to cause cross-user response poisoning, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to other users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of moderate impact was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped by a broad range of Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset components), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, OpenShift Container Platform and other Go-based components across Red Hat's portfolio. When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request that carries a non-empty request body, the body is written to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the desynchronized connection to the shared idle pool, and the trailing body bytes can be interpreted by the server as a subsequent pipelined request. A remote attacker able to send requests through a reverse proxy (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forwards CONNECT requests via a shared Transport could exploit this to poison the responses received by other users of the pooled connection, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to them. Red Hat rates this flaw MODERATE (CVSS 6.5, limited confidentiality and integrity impact with no availability impact), which is lower than the CISA score of 7.5 (IMPORTANT) based on a confidentiality-only vector; Red Hat's assessment reflects that the exposure requires a shared reverse-proxy deployment that forwards CONNECT requests with bodies and yields low confidentiality and integrity impact. For most affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred because the flaw is rated MODERATE severity with a CVSS score below 7.0, so the residual risk of cross-user response poisoning in such proxy deployments remains until a fix is delivered; for a subset of affected products fixes are being pursued by their maintaining teams, and some affected streams are out of active support.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can bypass connection-level flow control limits—mechanisms that regulate incoming network data—potentially causing excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS). This issue occurs because the server improperly refunds flow control credits twice for the same data: once when a client resets a stream, and again when the application reads the buffered data. notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because, while remote unauthenticated clients can bypass configured connection receive buffer thresholds on affected HTTP/2 servers, overall resource exhaustion remains bounded. Exploitation is constrained by stream-level flow controls and limits on concurrent streams, which prevents an attacker from causing unbounded memory consumption or a complete denial of service. Go-based network services handling untrusted HTTP/2 traffic may experience elevated memory usage under sustained reset attacks, but typical deployments remain operational without catastrophic service disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP server sends a successful response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request without taking raw control of the connection, it improperly continues to process incoming data as standard HTTP requests instead of establishing a tunnel. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior to conduct HTTP request smuggling through intermediate proxy servers, potentially bypassing security controls.

notes.text: net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate-impact flaw was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped in the golang and go-toolset components of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and used by many Go-based Red Hat products and components (including Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and bundled components such as osbuild-composer and rhc). When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve HTTP requests from a connection that should be treated as an opaque tunnel. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server through an intermediate proxy that treats the connection as tunneled can exploit this desynchronization to conduct HTTP request smuggling, potentially bypassing proxy-enforced security controls and accessing requests or responses intended for other users. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity (CVSS 3.1 base score 6.5, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N), reflecting the limited confidentiality and integrity impact. Because the impact is Moderate with a CVSS score below 7.0, fixes for the affected Red Hat products are currently deferred rather than scheduled for an immediate update, and the Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2.0.z streams are out of support scope. The residual risk of deferral is limited to HTTP request smuggling against servers that accept HTTP/1 CONNECT requests and are deployed behind an intermediate proxy.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the html/template package in Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS, an attack that executes malicious scripts in a user's browser) through improper output escaping. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state. Consequently, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, potentially allowing untrusted content to bypass template sanitization.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Go's html/template package, which is shipped and used across multiple Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and other components that build against the Go toolchain. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state upon entering a new expression. As a result, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, allowing a remote attacker to supply untrusted content through a template that bypasses html/template sanitization and executes malicious script in a victim's browser. Successful exploitation requires a victim user to visit a rendered page of a Go web application that interpolates attacker-controlled input into JavaScript template literals. Red Hat has rated this flaw MODERATE with a CVSS 3.1 score of 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N), consistent with the upstream assessment; the impact is limited to low confidentiality and integrity loss within the client browser context, with no availability impact. Because the CVSS score is below 7.0, the fix is deferred for the affected Red Hat product streams and update trackers are not being filed for this MODERATE severity flaw at this time. The residual risk is limited to Go-based web applications that render attacker-controlled content through html/template into JavaScript contexts; the flaw does not affect applications that do not use html/template with JavaScript template literals.

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable HTTP/2 server processing in affected Go applications by setting the environment variable GODEBUG=http2server=0, or restrict network exposure to trusted clients.

For applications managed by systemd, configure the environment variable by creating a service override:

systemctl edit <service-name>

Add the following lines under the [Service] section:

[Service]
Environment="GODEBUG=http2server=0"

Apply the changes and restart the daemon:

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart <service-name>

To limit network exposure using firewalld, restrict access to trusted networks:

firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted-ip-range> --permanent
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveats:
Disabling HTTP/2 forces incoming client traffic to HTTP/1.1 and will break protocols that require HTTP/2, such as gRPC.

Warning: Reloading systemd configurations and restarting the service or firewall will briefly interrupt active network sessions and cause temporary service unavailability.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. This vulnerability allows improper certificate validation, bypassing policy constraints via using ExtKeyUsageAny in VerifyOptions.KeyUsages.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is rated as an Important severity because the vulnerability was found in the certificate validation logic of the Verify function. When VerifyOptions.KeyUsages includes ExtKeyUsageAny, certificate chains containing policy graphs may bypass certificate policy validation. This flaw allows an attacker to trick the system into accepting an invalid certificate, potentially enabling spoofing attacks, the issue weakens trust decisions in affected cases and impacts system integrity. Confidentiality and availability are not affected.

cwe.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. The compiler fails to correctly check for integer overflow or underflow in arithmetic operations involving loop induction variables. As a result, the compiler allows invalid memory indexing to occur at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: possible memory corruption after bound check elimination
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is only exploitable in applications that contain a loop structure that relies on an induction variable. An induction variable is a variable that gets modified, usually incremented or decremented, by a predictable amount on each iteration. Inside the loop, the induction variable must be directly used as the index to access or modify elements within an array or a slice. Additionally, an attacker must be able to cause an integer overflow or underflow in the induction variable to trigger this issue. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this vulnerability, strictly sanitize and enforce bounds checking on any untrusted user input that influences loop counters, iteration limits, or memory indices. If there is no integer overflow or underflow, the out-of-bounds access cannot occur.

cwe.name: Expected Behavior Violation

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. A no-op interface conversion prevented the compiler from correctly identifying non-overlapping memory moves. As a result, the compiler allows unsafe memory move operations to occur at runtime, potentially causing data corruption, memory corruption or unexpected application behavior.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: no-op interface conversion bypasses overlap checking
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This issue is only exploitable in applications that contain a memory move or copy operation that is subject to a no-op (no-operation) interface conversion. Furthermore, the source and destination memory addresses involved in the move or copy must overlap and an attacker must be able to supply an input that triggers this specific operation. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw of moderate impact was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped by a broad range of Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset components), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, OpenShift Container Platform and other Go-based components across Red Hat's portfolio. When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request that carries a non-empty request body, the body is written to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the desynchronized connection to the shared idle pool, and the trailing body bytes can be interpreted by the server as a subsequent pipelined request. A remote attacker able to send requests through a reverse proxy (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forwards CONNECT requests via a shared Transport could exploit this to poison the responses received by other users of the pooled connection, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to them. Red Hat rates this flaw MODERATE (CVSS 6.5, limited confidentiality and integrity impact with no availability impact), which is lower than the CISA score of 7.5 (IMPORTANT) based on a confidentiality-only vector; Red Hat's assessment reflects that the exposure requires a shared reverse-proxy deployment that forwards CONNECT requests with bodies and yields low confidentiality and integrity impact. For most affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred because the flaw is rated MODERATE severity with a CVSS score below 7.0, so the residual risk of cross-user response poisoning in such proxy deployments remains until a fix is delivered; for a subset of affected products fixes are being pursued by their maintaining teams, and some affected streams are out of active support.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When operating as a reverse proxy, the HTTP/2 implementation does not properly validate framing-related headers in responses received from upstream servers before forwarding them to downstream HTTP/1 clients. A malicious upstream server can exploit this flaw by sending malformed response headers, resulting in HTTP response smuggling, where message boundaries between the proxy and client become desynchronized. This issue may allow attackers to bypass security controls, poison web caches, or intercept sensitive data from other user sessions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can bypass connection-level flow control limits—mechanisms that regulate incoming network data—potentially causing excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS). This issue occurs because the server improperly refunds flow control credits twice for the same data: once when a client resets a stream, and again when the application reads the buffered data. Consequently, a malicious client can exceed configured connection buffer limits.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass via double refund in HTTP/2 server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because, while remote unauthenticated clients can bypass configured connection receive buffer thresholds on affected HTTP/2 servers, overall resource exhaustion remains bounded. Exploitation is constrained by stream-level flow controls and limits on concurrent streams, which prevents an attacker from causing unbounded memory consumption or a complete denial of service. Go-based network services handling untrusted HTTP/2 traffic may experience elevated memory usage under sustained reset attacks, but typical deployments remain operational without catastrophic service disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.
